about: Golden set for retrieval quality on the Caching concept.
Each query is phrased the way a stuck learner would actually put it, not
as a keyword string -- that is the input retrieval will really receive.
`relevant` lists the chunk keys that genuinely answer the query. Keys are
stable across knowledge-base rebuilds; row ids are not.
Judgement calls are recorded in `note`. Anything ambiguous is written down
rather than left implicit, because a golden set nobody can audit is just a

queries.query: why would I put a cache in front of my database
queries.note: The motivation. Both the problem statement and the fix count.

queries.query: what actually is a cache
the database is answering the same question over and over
queries.note: Restates the opening problem in the learner's own words.

queries.query: how much faster is a cache really
why is reading from memory faster than reading from disk
what is a cache hit rate and why does it matter
my cached data is out of date after someone updates it
queries.note: Staleness. Step 4 explains it, explanation 5 says what to do.

queries.query: what do I give up by using a cache
is there data I should never cache
how long should something stay in the cache
what does TTL mean
should I delete the cached copy when the underlying data changes
increasing the cache size did not fix my stale data problem
queries.note: The point is that staleness is not a capacity problem.

queries.query: who is responsible for putting things into the cache
what is the cache-aside pattern
what should my code do on a cache miss
does the cache talk to the database by itself
queries.note: Step 6 makes the point that the cache is passive.

queries.query: a thousand requests hit the database the moment the key expired
what is a thundering herd
queries.note: The name for the same thing.

queries.query: how do I stop all my keys expiring at the same moment
only one request should refill the cache while the others wait
difference between write-through and write-back
queries.note: Not covered by the lesson at all -- the only source is the question explanation. Deliberately kept: it shows what retrieval does when the lesson has a gap.

queries.query: is a cache a kind of database
queries.note: Step 2 states it holds no truth of its own.

queries.query: what does a cache actually save me
queries.note: Ambiguous on purpose: both the repeated-work framing and the latency numbers are fair answers.
